newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
PUBJAB CHIEF MINISTER QUITS ON CONGRESS CHIEF'S DIKTAT

Punjab chief minister H.S. Brar submitted his resignation to Congress president Sitaram Kesri. Earlier, Kesri had asked Brar to step down and deputed four central party functionaries as observers to choose Brar's successor at a meeting of the Congress Legislature Party in Chandigarh. Party sources said deputy chief minister Rajinder Kaur Bhattal was likely to succeed Brar. Brar's removal appeared to have been done in view of the forthcoming Punjab assembly elections due early next year, sources added.
The Hindustan Times
PEACE EMERGES IN CONGRESS PARTY

A temporary truce between Congress chief Sitaram Kesri and former prime minister and Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader P. V. Narasimha Rao emerged with the latter pledging to implement the party's resolution on ties with the United Front (UF) government. Speaking at the CPP meeting, Rao ruled out any conflict between the Congress Working Committee and the CPP. Rao attacked the UF, asking it to toe the Congress line or face the axe, in a bid to assuage the hurt temper of the party chief. Financial Express
LEFT ATTACKS UNITED FRONT ON ECONOMIC ISSUES

The Left Front attacked the United Front government for deviating from the common minimum programme (CMP) in relation to economic policies. The Front's steering committee asked the government to supply rice and wheat to people living below the poverty line at half the public distribution system price in line with its pledge in the CMP. The Left leaders also criticised the government for carrying on with the previous regime's policies on issues like disinvestment of public sector units' shares and opening up of insurance sector to multinational companies.
BPL VALUES PAGING ARM AT $200 MLN

BPL Cellular Holdings, entering the American Depository Receipt (ADR) market, is learnt to have pegged its paging services licence at $200 million. This makes BPL the world's most expensive enterprise of its kind. The nearest acquisition price compared to BPL is $188 million for the U.S.-based Gold Coast Paging with 3.65 million subscribers. In comparision, BPL Cellular had 1,935 subscribers on March 31, 1996. The total asset value of BPL Cellular Holdings' paging licence is around $198 million, representing 20 percent of the $1 billion value placed on BPL Cellular for its coming ADR issue.
BPL MOBILE MOOTS RIVAL ROAMING CONSORTIUM

Bombay based BPL Mobile Communications is entering into an alliance with cellular operators in three other cities. The company plans to form a network for providing roaming facility to their customers. The alliance will consist of BPL Mobile in Bombay, Usha Martin in Calcutta, Essar Telecom in Delhi and SkyCell in Madras. The four operators were left out of the World One consortium that was formed to offer similar services. World One consists of Hutchison Max in Bombay, Airtel in Delhi, Birla- AT&T in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Goa, Escotel in Haryana, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh, Hexacom in Rajasthan, Modicom in Punjab and Karnataka, Modi-Telstra in Calcutta, RPG Cellular in Madras and Tata
UNION BANK OF SWITZERLAND ALLOWED TO SET UP BROKING ARM

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board has cleared the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) proposal for setting up a stock broking firm, UBS Securities Ltd (USIL). USIL will be a 100 percent subsidiary of UBS and its equity base will be around 300 million rupees. Of this, 75 percent will be funded by UBS and the rest by non resident Indians (NRIs). Like other Foreign Institutional Investors, USIL is seeking NRI participation (25 percent) to fulfil the Finance Ministry's mandatory requirements for setting up a stock broking firm.
OSWAL PLANS 29 BLN RUPEES EXPANSION PLANS

The Oswal group has drawn a 29 billion rupee expansion plan for its fertiliser manufacturing capacity over the next three years. The group plans to invest another three billion rupees to modernise its existing petrochemicals and LDPE business. Group chairman Abhey Oswal claimed the entire investment would be made without any fresh injection of equity through a rights or public issue. The group plans to fund the new projects through internal accruals and term loans. Oswal Chemicals and Fertilizers Ltd, a group company, has decided to put up a 16 billion rupee grass-root naptha-based ammonia/urea plant at Paradeep Port in Orissa.
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH RATE DECLINES

Industrial growth during the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) dipped to 4.8 percent as against 12.8 percent in the previous corresponding period. The infrastructure sector grew by 3.3 percent as compared to 10.7 percent in the previous year. As per the growth rates of 24 select industries released by the government, the electricity sector, with 11.4 percent weightage in the index of industrial production (IIP), showed a 2.6 percent growth (10.9 percent). The index includes 24 sectors accounting for 50.4 percent of the overall IIP. Crude petroleum posted a poor 10.3 percent growth (15.8 percent). The Economic Times
TURNOVER OF DUNLOP GOES UP BY 22 PCT

Dunlop India Ltd reported an improved result with a 295 percent rise in profits before tax at 212.7 million rupees for the six months ended September 1996. The company achieved a 22 percent growth in turnover at 3.36 billion rupees. Total expenditure amounted to 2.99 billion rupees compared to 2.57 billion rupees during the corresponding period of the previous year. The gross profit stood at 243.6 billion rupees against 83.1 million rupees in the previous period.
APEX BANK MAY BE ALLOWED TO APPROVE LONG TERM ECBS

The Finance Ministry plans to delegate additional powers to the central bank (RBI) to sanction the external commercial borrowings (ECBs) for longer maturities than the current three year limit. Until now, the corporates seeking to raise ECBs beyond the three-year limit had to seek the Finance Ministry's permission. This will enable the RBI to raise the internal cap of $500 million on the total amount of ECBs maturity up to three years. It is learnt that the stipulated rules do not apply to companies borrowing from foreign institutional investors operating in the country.
UNITED FRONT PANEL OPPOSES PETRO-GOODS PRICE HIKE

The prime minister's move to hike petroleum prices has been put down by the United Front (UF) steering committee. The matter figured in the proceedings of the steering committee today. The UF constituents were not moved by prime minister and the Finance Minister's emphasis on the urgency to reduce the reduce the oil pool deficit and opposed the proposal to raise oil prices. The UF panel's stand rules out any immediate hike in the prices of the petroleum products as the prime minister has already stated any decision on the matter was contingent on a consensus among the UF partners.
Business Standard
LACK OF CONSENSUS MAY STALL BROADCASTING BILLS

The broadcast and Prasar Bharati amendment bills are unlikely to be passed in the current session of parliament. The all-party consensus sought by the government on the matter has failed to emerge. A majority of the parties are undecided over whether joint ventures by Indian nationals/companies with foreign equity exceeding 15 percent individually or 20 percent in the aggregate should get the nod to broadcast. The Prasar Bharati Amendment Bill aims to corporatise Doordarshan (state owned TV channel) and All India Radio. The Indian Broadcasting Bill aims to regulate private radio and TV broadcasting, including direct-to-home networks and multichannel microwave distribution system.
FISCAL DEFICIT PUT AT 5.4 PCT OF GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT

Efforts to cap fiscal deficit at five percent of gross domestic product in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) may suffer as the current forcasts put the deficit at 5.3 to 5.4 percent. The slippage was attributed to an anticipated shortfall in divestment proceeds, uncertain revenue targets and rise in defence spendings. Government sources said efforts were on to check any excess outgo under subsidies. They said the increase in prices of food sold through public distribution outlets was likely to keep the food subsidy bill within 52 billion rupees.
APEX BANK PROBING ADVANCES MADE BY FOREIGN AND PRIVATE BANKS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) launched investigations into all advances sanctioned by the boards of foreign and private sector banks. RBI sources said the central bank was examining whether the approvals had been made as per the RBI norms on lending. The loan portfolios of the foreign and the private banks were more risk-prone than that of the nationalised banks, sources added. The RBI had never examined the approvals made at the chairman's level earlier.
The Observer
BILL TO RESOLVE DISPUTES WITH MULTINATIONALS IN INDIA SOON

A new bill on judicial reforms will be introduced in the current session of parliament. This bill aims to set up more Lok Nyayalayas and Lok Adalats (people's courts) to support the overburdened judicial system, where more than 25 million cases are pending. This was stated by union minister of state for law and justice R.D. Khalap at the National Conference on Judicial Reforms organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry in Delhi. Khalap hinted at another important bill, the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, which would facilitate the resolution of commercial disputes among multinationals and domestic corporates in India.
REGULATORY NORMS MOOTED FOR NON BANKING FINANCE COMPANIES

The proposed company bill, likely to be moved in the next budget session of parliament, will overhaul the Companies Act. According to sources in the Company Law Board, the new bill will have exclusive regulatory provisions for the non-banking finance companies (NBFCs), specially the NBFCs having dubious distinction as private limited companies. The central bank (RBI) has asked the Finance Ministry to make it mandatory for NBFCs to register themselves with the apex bank. The RBI and the government were concerned about the fact that during the last five years, NBFCs were able to raise total public equity worth about 500 billion rupees. EXPORTS TO PICK UP IN OCTOBER-MARCH

Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said exports would pick up in the second half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The minister said exports between April and September registered a growth rate of 9.9 percent in dollar terms and 21.9 percent in rupee terms. Although the half-yearly export growth of 9.9 percent was lower than the targeted growth of 18-20 percent, Ramaiah said this had been achieved on a higher base of the previous year. The items showing high growth rates were electronic goods, cotton yarn, raw cotton, wool, coffee as well as agro and allied products, the minister said.
UNITED FRONT DIVIDED ON REFORMS

The United Front steering committee failed to end the stalemate on the vexed question of the pace of economic reforms. Despite severe criticism from the Left parties attending the crucial meeting, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram refused to withdraw the Insurance Amendment Bill, to be introduced in the winter session of parliament. The bill would pave the way for foreign participation in the insurance sector. Chidambaram and Industry Minister Murasoli Maran also reaffirmed the role of public sector units in the economy and assured the Left parties that steps would be taken to revive sick units.
